proposer.mechanism: ADVERSE-TICK-FLOW SKIP gate, layered on position-tier-gate (cap=1) verbatim. On each on_order() for an OPEN that survives the cap=1 gate, read the most recent quote from cache.quote_tick(instrument_id) and the mid 100ms earlier (from a small rolling buffer of quote ticks maintained in on_quote_tick). Compute signed_mom_100 = (mid_now - mid_100ms_ago) in tick units, signed so that positive = same direction as the OPEN (BUY -> mid up, SELL -> mid down). If signed_mom_100 <= adverse_tick_threshold (default -1.0 ticks, i.e. the market just moved at least 1 tick AGAINST the OPEN direction in the last 100ms) AND current_spread_ticks <= spread_max (default 1.0 tick), SKIP the OPEN. Otherwise SUBMIT. CLOSE (is_reduce_only) orders always submit unchanged. Subscribe to quote_ticks in on_start() lazily on first order seen.
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: Empirically measured (via analysis skill on the 12-date train window, base algo positions.csv joined with MBP-1 quotes): when the market has just moved >=1 tick AGAINST the OPEN direction in the past 100ms AND the spread is at its 1-tick floor, the resulting trades have NEGATIVE aggregate PnL ($-586.00 over 11,907 trades = -$0.049/trade, win_rate ~31%). This subset is 13.2% of base trades. Skipping it leaves $4,844.50 vs base $4,258.50 = +13.76% improvement, comfortably exceeding the +5% pass gate. The mechanism: in tight-spread regimes (low information, MES default state), a sharp 100ms adverse tick BEFORE the oracle's OPEN is evidence that the oracle is reacting to a transient price excursion and is about to be wrong about the 30s direction. In wide-spread regimes the signal flips (wide spread = news / volatility burst where oracle has real edge), which is why the rule is GATED on tight-spread to avoid throwing out the profitable wide-spread tail. The dropped subset has aggregate PnL clearly below the -$213 break-even-for-gate threshold (-$586 << -$213), so this is a robust signal rather than a coin-flip threshold.
proposer.why_survives_costs: Mean slippage stays 0 and commissions stay 0 in this simulator (verified from base backtest-results.json: total_commissions=0.0, mean_slippage=0.0). The mechanism only adds a SKIP condition on OPENs - no order construction, no order modification, no new order types. CLOSE orders submit unchanged so intraday_flat compliance is preserved. The only added runtime work is maintaining a rolling 100ms quote buffer and a constant-time comparison per OPEN - negligible.
proposer.builds_on: position-tier-gate (cap=1 retained verbatim as the first gate; adverse-tick filter is an additive SKIP gate applied AFTER cap=1 passes, only for OPEN orders). Materially different from prior PC runs: r1 (consensus filter) was inert with no empirical grounding; r2 (loss-cooldown) had no empirical grounding for the 1-2s loss-clustering premise and the analysis showed losses are nearly i.i.d.; r3 (winners-run skip-close) suffered selection-bias (duration-PnL correlation was caused BY oracle confidence, not by holding duration). This proposal is grounded in a measured 12-date analysis showing the SKIP subset has CONCRETE negative aggregate PnL, not a correlation that requires extrapolation. The rule uses only on-OPEN-time-observable microstructure features (current quote + 100ms back), so no look-ahead.
proposer.alternatives_considered: (1) signed_mom_100 <= -1t alone (no spread gate): drops 16.0% of trades, kept=$4375.00 = +2.74% delta — CLOSE not PASS. Adding spread<=1t makes the dropped subset more concentrated in true losers because wide-spread OPENs are systematically positive-EV regardless of micro-momentum. (2) signed_mom_500 / 1000 / 2000 instead of 100ms: longer lookbacks DEGRADE PnL when used as SKIP signals — the negative-PnL subset is specifically the very recent (100ms) adverse-flow set. Longer-horizon adverse flow includes legitimate trends where oracle is correct. (3) Imbalance-only (signed_imb <= -0.7): drops 10.8% but sum is +$313 - dropping positive-EV trades; rejected. (4) far_side_size as a KEEP signal: when far-side liquidity is very thin (size <= 4) the trades have HIGHER mean PnL ($0.13 vs $0.047), implying we should NOT skip those even when mom_100 looks adverse. Adding ' & far_side_sz>=5' to the SKIP rule gave +13.94% — slightly stronger than the spread version but introduces book-size sensitivity that may be more regime-fragile. Spread is the more parsimonious gating feature. Reserved for r5 if needed. (5) mom_100<=-1t & mom_500<=-1t (sustained adverse): drops 13.3%, delta=+8.15% — weaker than the spread-gated version. (6) The criticizer-suggested asymmetric-extension and protective-stop ideas have already been tried (r3) or shown to be inert (loss distribution too tight, per r3 NOTES). (7) Microstructure SIZE-AWARE filters (cap=1+sizing): the cap=1 framework precludes real sizing changes (skip/submit only). (8) Increasing position cap (cap=2,3): empirically inert per base NOTES (oracle never exceeds 1 contract).

objections.text: Look-ahead-bias risk via ts_opened in the empirical analysis. The Proposer's empirical justification computed signed_mom_100 = mid(ts_open) - mid(ts_open - 100ms) using positions['ts_opened'] - i.e. the fill timestamp. In the deterministic replay, ts_opened is the OPEN's fill timestamp, NOT the moment the strategy issued the OPEN order. The on_order() hook in the exec algo fires at order INIT time, which is some quote ticks EARLIER than the fill. The analysis therefore measured quotes UP TO AND INCLUDING the tick that filled the order - which can post-date the strategy's decision to issue the order. This may inflate the predictive power of the 100ms lookback because some of those 100ms quotes include the impact of the order in flight (or at least the same tick that caused the fill). In production, the algo at on_order() sees quotes only up to the order's ts_init, which is strictly earlier than ts_opened. Suggest re-running the empirical evaluation using a timestamp closer to ts_init (or fills.csv's ts_init field, which corresponds to the order's emission time at the strategy, not the venue's fill time). If the +13.76% effect mostly survives, the hypothesis is sound; if it collapses, the rule is partly capturing fill-tick information that won't be available at decision time.

Regime fragility / per-date stability. The per-date breakdown shows the rule HURTS PnL on 5/12 train dates (20260308 -65.75, 20260309 -229.25, 20260310 -96.00, 20260311 -95.00, 20260312 -97.50) and HELPS on 7/12 dates with the help concentrated in the late-window choppy/high-volume days (20260316 +209.75, 20260317 +167.75, 20260318 +91.50, 20260319 +77.00, 20260320 +101.00). Net is +$586 only because the help-days dominate by magnitude. If the test window (or future OOS) has a more 'quiet-volume' profile like 20260308-20260312, the rule REGRESSES PnL vs base. The training aggregate masks a regime-dependent edge. Either the rule needs a regime detector (only activate on high-volume days), or the Proposer should acknowledge that the +13.76% train-window number overstates expected OOS performance and the realistic expectation is closer to +5-8%. Still likely a PASS in expectation but with substantially wider variance than the headline number suggests.

Implementation: cache.quote_tick() returns only the latest quote, not a 100ms-old quote. The Proposer correctly identifies that a manual rolling buffer in on_quote_tick is needed. But: (a) the buffer needs to retain quotes spanning >= 100ms but not be unboundedly large in active periods (MES sees ~10k+ quotes per second during volatile bursts). Need a deque with size cap that prunes by timestamp, not by length. (b) When on_order fires and we need 'the mid 100ms ago,' we must search the buffer for the quote whose ts_event <= now - 100_000_000 ns - this is an O(log n) bisect on a deque, doable. (c) Subscription must happen before any quote arrives. Lazy subscription in on_order won't capture the earliest quotes - but for the first few seconds of the session there will be no signal anyway (no OPENs yet, no buffer history). Acceptable but document. (d) If quote_tick() returns None at decision time (rare but possible at session start), the safe default must be SUBMIT (don't skip). Specify these as load-bearing details, not optional polish.

Threshold-fit / specificity risk. The values 'mom_100 <= -1.0 ticks' and 'spread <= 1.0 tick' were selected from a grid search of (mom lookback, mom threshold, spread threshold). The search yielded several PASS-candidates with similar magnitudes (mom_100<=-1 & spread<=1t: +13.76%; mom_100<=-1 & far_side_sz>=5: +13.94%; mom_100<=-1 & mom_500<=-1: +8.15%). Multiple plausible rules at similar headline numbers is a classic overfit signature - the train-window optimum is not necessarily the test-window optimum. Mitigation: the headline rule is grounded in a clean economic story (tight-spread + adverse-tick = oracle reacting to transient pop, no edge); the dropped subset's aggregate is clearly negative (-$586 vs the gate-break-even of -$213, a margin of >2x); and the alternatives are not radically better. Acceptable but the realistic expected OOS uplift is more like 60-70% of the headline 13.76%, i.e. +8-10%. Still likely PASS.

Spread = 1 tick is the modal MES state (>=66%/73% of all OPENs per the analysis). 'spread<=1t' is therefore almost equivalent to 'spread==1t' since the tick floor IS 1 tick. The 'wide-spread is positive-EV regardless' carve-out is a real protection but the rule effectively says: in the dominant regime, skip on adverse 100ms tick. Worth ensuring the spread comparison handles MES's 0.25 tick correctly: spread_price <= TICK_SIZE * 1.0 = 0.25, in price terms not ticks. Implementation detail.

100ms is a short measurement window. MES quotes update very frequently in active sessions but can have multi-second gaps in quiet sessions. If no quote update has arrived in the past 100ms (i.e. mid_100ms_ago is the same quote as mid_now), the buffer will return mid_then = mid_now and signed_mom_100 = 0 - the SKIP condition fails (>-1.0 threshold) and the OPEN submits. This is correct (no recent flow signal = don't skip), but means the rule is silently disabled in quiet regimes - which actually matches the per-date pattern: quiet days have less skipping. Acceptable; no change needed.

suggested_alternatives: Verify the look-ahead concern by re-computing signed_mom_100 using the order's ts_init (from fills.csv) rather than position's ts_opened. If +13.76% drops by >50% in this corrected analysis, the headline overstates the edge and the threshold may need re-tuning. If it survives, the rule is sound.

Consider falling back to a more conservative threshold (e.g. mom_100 <= -1.5 ticks) that is less common but more strongly net-negative in the dropped subset. Trade-off: less activation but more robust expected uplift per skip.

Document the per-date variability prominently in NOTES.md so the Backtest Observations section can verify whether the live aggregate matches the analysis-predicted pattern (helping on choppy days, hurting on quiet days).
criticizer.reasoning: The hypothesis is grounded in real empirical analysis (a marked improvement over r1's and r2's pre-implementation analytic gaps) and the dropped subset's negative aggregate is robust enough to clear the gate with margin. But the look-ahead concern via ts_opened is a real, falsifiable risk to the headline number, and the per-date breakdown shows substantial regime fragility that the headline aggregate masks. These are not BLOCKING - the rule is logically coherent and bounded in failure (worst case is PnL drop without slippage/commission regression) - but they need to be verified or acknowledged before implementation, not after. Revise to either re-validate without the ts_opened bias OR explicitly state in the hypothesis that the analysis is on fill-time approximations and the expected OOS uplift is materially less than the headline.
